source.author: verg
source.text: Has omnes, ubi mille rotam volvere per annos, Lethaeum ad fluvium deus evocat agmine magno, scilicet immemores supera ut convexa revisant, rursus et incipiant in corpora velle reverti.
source.text_original: Has omnes, ubi mille rotam volvere per annos, / Lethaeum ad fluvium deus evocat agmine magno, / scilicet immemores supera ut convexa revisant, / rursus et incipiant in corpora velle reverti.'
source.text_english: All these, when once they have rolled the wheel through a thousand years, a god summons in a great company to the Lethean river, so that, forgetful, they may revisit the upper vault of heaven, and may again begin to long to return into bodies.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quod quidem et Virgilius in sexto Aeneidos volumine sequens loquitur: Has omnes, ubi mille rotam volvere per annos, Lethaeum ad fluvium Deus evocat agmine magno; Scilicet immemores supera ut convexa revisant, Rursus et incipiant in corpora velle reverti.
reuse.text_original: Quod quidem et Virgilius in sexto Aeneidos volumine sequens loquitur: Has omnes, ubi mille rotam volvere per annos, Lethaeum ad fluvium Deus evocat agmine magno; Scilicet immemores supera ut convexa revisant, Rursus et incipiant in corpora velle reverti.
reuse.text_english: Virgil also says this in the sixth book of the Aeneid, following the same idea: All these souls, when a thousand years have rolled the wheel of time, God summons in a great company to the river Lethe, so that, forgetful, they may look again upon the upper realms of heaven, and once more begin to desire to return into bodies.
